title: Pay Now or at Checkout?
prerequisites: Knows present simple statements with pay.
observable_outcome: Ask when payment happens, understand the answer, then confirm the payment time.
learning_objective: Use Do I pay + option A + or + option B? to check a payment procedure and confirm the answer.

scenario.prompt: Your room is booked. Reception has not said when payment happens.
scenario.model: Do I pay now or at checkout?

language.grammar: Do + subject + base verb forms a present simple question. After do, use pay, not paying.
language.meaning: The speaker asks which of two payment times or procedures applies.
language.appropriateness: This direct choice question is suitable when both options seem possible. Should I pay...? is also common when asking what the hotel expects.
language.time_phrase: At checkout means during the hotel leaving-and-billing stage. Here, now means before the stay begins.

activities.prompt: Which sentence clearly checks the procedure?

options.text: Do I pay now or at checkout?
options.feedback: Yes. Do starts the question, pay stays in the base form, and both times are clear.

options.text: I pay now or at checkout.
options.feedback: This has statement word order. Use Do I pay...? to ask the question.

options.text: Do I paying now or at checkout?
options.feedback: After do, use the base verb pay, not paying.

activities.prompt: Reception says, 'At checkout.' What does that answer tell you?

options.feedback: Yes. Hotel checkout is the stage when a guest leaves and settles the bill.
No. That would mean pay now. At checkout points to the leaving stage.
No. The answer gives the payment time. It does not remove the payment.

activities.prompt: Which reply confirms what you understood?

options.text: Thanks. I'll pay when I check out.
options.feedback: Yes. It acknowledges the answer and restates the payment time.

options.text: Thanks. I paid when I checked out.
options.feedback: That describes a completed past event. Your stay has not happened yet.
No. Reception described payment timing, not whether checkout is optional.

transfer.situation: At a cafe, you do not know whether to pay at the counter or at your table.
transfer.task: Write one two-option question. Then add one short confirmation for the answer: 'At the counter.'
acceptable_responses: Do I pay at the counter or at the table? Thanks. I'll pay at the counter.
Should I pay at the counter or at the table? Okay, at the counter.
Do we pay here or at the table? Thanks, we'll pay here.
rubric: The question checks a real procedure.

review_prompt: Tomorrow, complete and answer: Do I pay ___ or ___?

visual.alt_text: A hotel journey runs from arrival to stay to checkout. A choice path compares paying now at arrival with paying later at checkout, then joins at a confirmation step.
visual.text_equivalent: ARRIVAL: pay now? | STAY | CHECKOUT: pay later? -> ASK: Do I pay now or at checkout? -> CONFIRM: I'll pay when I check out.

sources.title: Question forms
sources.coverage: Present simple questions use do before the subject and the infinitive form of the verb.

sources.title: checkout
sources.coverage: Hotel checkout is when a guest leaves after paying and returning a key.
sources.limitations: Dictionary definition; hotel practices can vary.

sources.title: pay
sources.coverage: Pay means giving money for goods or services.
